description: Global software-defined networking for Google Cloud resources.
detail: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) provides isolated, global private networks for Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Run, and managed services. Teams use it to define subnets, routes, firewall policies, private connectivity, and IP addressing across regions while keeping workloads on Google's backbone.
benefits: Global network with regional subnets
Granular routing, firewall, and IP address controls
Private connectivity for Google Cloud and hybrid workloads
cons: Requires careful IP address and route planning
Misconfigured firewall rules can block valid traffic or expose workloads
useCases: Isolating production, staging, and shared-service networks
Running private GKE and Compute Engine workloads
example: A SaaS company creates separate VPCs for production and development, connects them through a shared services hub, and applies firewall policies so only approved service ports are reachable.

description: Global and regional load balancing for applications and services.
detail: Cloud Load Balancing distributes HTTP(S), TCP, SSL proxy, UDP, and internal traffic across backends. It supports global anycast front ends, health checks, autoscaling integrations, Cloud CDN, Cloud Armor, and private service delivery patterns.
benefits: Global front ends with a single anycast IP
Built-in health checks and backend failover
Works with Cloud CDN, Cloud Armor, GKE, Compute Engine, and serverless backends
cons: Several load balancer types require correct selection up front
Advanced routing and certificate setup can add operational complexity
example: An ecommerce platform uses an external Application Load Balancer with managed certificates, Cloud CDN, and Cloud Armor to serve customers globally while failing over unhealthy backends.

description: Content delivery network for cacheable web and media content.
detail: Cloud CDN caches static and dynamic cacheable content at Google's edge locations. It integrates with external Application Load Balancers and backend services to reduce latency, lower origin load, and improve availability for global users.
benefits: Lower latency for global users
Reduced origin traffic and serving cost
Integrated with Google Cloud load balancing and security controls
cons: Best results require cache-aware application design
Cache invalidation and TTL settings must be managed carefully
useCases: Accelerating images, scripts, downloads, and static assets
Reducing origin load during traffic spikes
Serving web applications to distributed users
example: A training site uses Cloud CDN in front of Cloud Storage and an Application Load Balancer so course videos and assets load quickly for students in different regions.

description: Managed authoritative DNS on Google's infrastructure.
detail: Cloud DNS hosts public and private DNS zones with low-latency serving, APIs, IAM controls, DNSSEC support, and integration with VPC private name resolution. It is used to manage production domains, internal service names, and hybrid DNS patterns.
benefits: Reliable managed DNS with API and CLI automation
Supports public and private zones
Integrates with VPC and hybrid name resolution
cons: DNS design mistakes can affect every dependent service
Split-horizon and hybrid DNS require disciplined naming conventions
useCases: Managing private names for internal services
Automating DNS changes in deployment pipelines
example: A platform team manages private zones for internal APIs and public zones for customer-facing domains, applying IAM so only deployment automation can change production records.

description: Managed outbound internet access for private resources.
detail: Cloud NAT lets private Compute Engine and GKE workloads reach the internet for updates and external APIs without assigning external IP addresses. It is managed, scalable, and configured at the VPC and Cloud Router level.
benefits: Keeps workloads private while allowing controlled egress
No NAT instances to patch or scale
Works with Cloud Router and VPC routes
cons: Only handles outbound connections and return traffic
Port allocation and logging settings need review for high-scale workloads
useCases: Allowing private VMs to download patches
Giving private GKE nodes outbound access
Reducing exposure from public IP addresses
example: A security-conscious team removes external IPs from its worker nodes and uses Cloud NAT for package updates and outbound API calls.

description: Encrypted IPsec VPN connectivity for hybrid networks.
detail: Cloud VPN connects Google Cloud VPC networks to on-premises or other cloud networks over IPsec tunnels. HA VPN provides high availability with multiple interfaces and dynamic routing through Cloud Router.
benefits: Encrypted connectivity over the public internet
High-availability design options
Useful for quick hybrid or multicloud connections
cons: Throughput and latency depend on internet path quality
Less predictable than dedicated interconnect options
useCases: Connecting branch offices to Google Cloud
example: A company uses HA VPN and dynamic routing to connect a regional office to private services running in a Google Cloud VPC.

description: Dedicated or partner-assisted private connectivity to Google Cloud.
detail: Cloud Interconnect provides private, high-throughput connectivity between on-premises networks and Google Cloud. Dedicated Interconnect uses physical connections to Google, while Partner Interconnect uses supported service providers for flexible capacity and locations.
benefits: Private connectivity with more predictable performance
High bandwidth options for enterprise workloads
Can reduce reliance on public internet paths
cons: Requires network provider coordination and lead time
Costs and redundancy design are higher than simple VPN setups
useCases: Private access from data centers to Google Cloud
example: A bank uses redundant Dedicated Interconnect links to connect its data centers to Google Cloud with predictable latency for core application traffic.

description: Private access to Google, third-party, and producer services.
detail: Private Service Connect lets consumers privately access services over internal IP addresses while service producers publish managed endpoints. It supports private access to Google APIs, third-party services, and internal services across VPC boundaries.
benefits: Private service access without exposing traffic to the public internet
Clear producer and consumer network separation
Works well for managed service and shared platform patterns
cons: Endpoint and DNS design must be planned
Service publishing patterns can be unfamiliar for smaller teams
example: A platform team publishes a payments API through Private Service Connect so application teams can consume it privately from separate VPCs.

description: Central hub for managing enterprise network connectivity.
detail: Network Connectivity Center provides a hub-and-spoke model for connecting VPCs, on-premises networks, branch locations, and other clouds. It helps teams simplify topology management, routing, and operational visibility across distributed networks.
benefits: Centralizes hybrid and multicloud connectivity
Supports scalable hub-and-spoke architecture
Improves operational consistency for large networks
cons: Requires clear routing and segmentation strategy
Can be more capability than small deployments need
useCases: Connecting branch offices and cloud VPCs
example: A multinational organization uses Network Connectivity Center as a central hub for regional VPCs, data centers, and branch networks.

description: DDoS defense and web application firewall for internet-facing apps.
detail: Cloud Armor protects applications behind supported Google Cloud load balancers with DDoS mitigation, WAF rules, preconfigured protections, rate limiting, geo controls, and adaptive protection features.
benefits: Edge-based DDoS and WAF protection
Preconfigured and custom security rules
Integrates with external Application Load Balancers
cons: Rules must be tested to avoid blocking valid users
Advanced policies require ongoing tuning
example: A media site uses Cloud Armor preconfigured WAF rules and rate limiting to reduce malicious traffic before requests reach application backends.

description: Next-generation firewall controls for Google Cloud workloads.
detail: Cloud NGFW provides distributed firewall capabilities, hierarchical firewall policies, threat prevention options, and granular network security controls for VPC workloads. It helps enforce consistent segmentation and protection across projects and environments.
benefits: Centralized firewall policy management
Granular segmentation for cloud workloads
Advanced threat prevention options
cons: Policy hierarchy requires governance
Advanced inspection features can add cost and design considerations
useCases: Adding intrusion prevention to cloud networks
example: A regulated business uses hierarchical firewall policies to enforce baseline deny rules across projects while allowing application teams to manage approved local rules.

description: Network observability, diagnostics, and topology analysis.
detail: Network Intelligence Center helps teams visualize topology, test connectivity, inspect firewall reachability, monitor performance, and troubleshoot network issues across Google Cloud environments.
benefits: Improves visibility into complex cloud networks
Helps diagnose routing and firewall issues
Supports proactive network operations
cons: Insights depend on available telemetry and logging
Teams still need networking expertise to act on findings
example: An operations team uses Connectivity Tests before deploying firewall updates, reducing outages caused by unintended rule changes.
